claims.claim: In the same study the two detectors disagreed substantially, GPTZero classifying 156 English articles as AI-generated and Binoculars 96, with an overlap of 45.
claims.page: Section 5, Trends in Pages Flagged for AI

claims.claim: Russell, Karpinska and Iyyer measured that the majority vote among five expert annotators misclassifies only one of three hundred articles.
claims.source: Jenna Russell, Marzena Karpinska & Mohit Iyyer, ACL 2025

claims.claim: In the same study the experts' explanations named AI vocabulary as the most common giveaway.
claims.page: Section on what expert annotators focus on

claims.claim: The same study reports that formulaic sentence and document structures, its example being optimistically vague conclusions, come close behind vocabulary as a clue for the expert annotators.
claims.page: Section on what expert annotators focus on

claims.claim: The same study observed that neither paraphrasing nor humanization effectively removes all of these signatures.
claims.page: Section on what expert annotators focus on

claims.claim: The same r/worldbuilding rule extends the ban to using AI merely to organise, edit, present or rewrite the poster's own worldbuilding material.
claims.source: r/worldbuilding moderators, subreddit rules wiki, rule 4
claims.quote: Using AI to organize, edit, present, or rewrite material

claims.claim: TTRPG historian Shannon Appelcline, having read five paragraphs of an LLM-written designer history, says the false implications created between sentences were worse than the outright factual errors.
claims.source: Shannon Appelcline, email to Rascal News, quoted by Lin Codega
claims.page: Appelcline's emailed statement, roughly one-third in

claims.claim: Reporter Lin Codega describes the AI-generated designer profiles as flattening careers into sycophantic textual formulas.
claims.quote: a sloppish wasteland of sycophantic textual formulas

claims.claim: Codega reports that every AI-written reply followed the same four-move formula: apology, rewrite, nebulous statement of future intent, then a shift of the goalposts.
claims.quote: each explanatory message followed a similar formula
claims.page: section on her Facebook interview with 4 Pillar

claims.claim: A commenter on that review says machines tend to have a particular style of palaver, while conceding the signs are subtle and can be missed once a human has edited the text.
claims.quote: machines do tend to have a particular style of palaver

claims.claim: A commenter maintains that LLMs do not write like intelligent humans once the text reaches any serious length, and that the hard case is telling good LLM text from a dull human's.
claims.quote: LLMs do not write like intelligent humans

claims.claim: The same commenter holds that the tell is length-dependent, because a model that cannot juggle interconnected concepts or reason about consequences eventually reveals itself.
claims.quote: If it goes on long enough, it always shows itself.

claims.claim: Mike Shea, a full-time D&D prep writer, says that in his experience LLMs are not great for generating game content compared with reading books and using his imagination.
claims.quote: not great for generating game content
claims.page: section 'Your Best Large Language Model – Your Brain'

claims.claim: Leon Furze reports that when he pointed GPT-4 at a broad exoplanet catalogue for his science-fiction worldbuilding, the model returned a generic response, and that linking one specific catalogue entry was what made the description specific.
A member of the Obsidian Portal campaign-wiki forum, answering a request for AI-generated wiki text for NPCs and locations, replies that AI generation is not all that imaginative in what it provides.
claims.source: forum member 'ElMuggs', Obsidian Portal community forums
claims.quote: not all that 'imaginative' in what it provides
